milestone.title: Autopilot prompt-delivery stability — runner readiness gate + lifecycle stall threshold + chat-driven ergonomics

intent.outcome: The autopilot pipeline (mp autopilot start) reliably drives a runner through to AC verification end-to-end, with three concrete defects fixed: (1) the runner readiness gate waits for the harness to be idle before delivering the prompt; (2) the lifecycle poller's stall threshold no longer trips while the runner is still working; (3) chat operators get a wait verb that blocks until complete and a tail --follow verb that streams the runner's recent activity.

problem.description: M236 dogfood (chat-driven autopilot emulation, commit 2646458) and the parallel herdr-orc cycle in pane w18:t2 surfaced three concrete defects that prevent the autopilot from driving a milestone to complete from the chat. (1) The orchestrator's runner-prompt dispatch does not wait for the harness to be interactive_ready: true — the prompt can land while OpenCode's TUI is still booting, where the harness never sees it. (2) The lifecycle poller's stall threshold is too tight — a slow-but-working runner (e.g., a 5-minute cargo build) trips the stalled lifecycle before the work is done. (3) Chat operators have no clean wait / tail verbs: the current mp autopilot status is a snapshot, not a stream, and watching the activity.json file by hand is fragile. Without these, the autopilot's chat-driven workflow is bounded by real-time race conditions rather than being a stable, observable execution.

in_scope: WP1 — Runner-readiness gate. In crates/mp/src/autopilot/drive/bridge.rs (or wherever the runner prompt is dispatched), insert a wait_for_runner_idle(grace_ms) call before delivering the prompt. Default grace is 5000 ms; configurable via the existing mp autopilot start config. Add a unit test that proves the gate fires before delivery by stubbing the runner's interactive_ready response. Add a regression test that runs the full pipeline on a fake runner and asserts the prompt is queued, not yet sent, until the gate clears.

WP2 — Lifecycle poller stall threshold. In crates/mp/src/autopilot/drive/state_machine.rs, tune the default stall window from 30 min to a more reasonable value (proposed: 5 min default, 15 min ceiling). Add a config knob agent.automation.stall_timeout_minutes so projects can override per their runner's typical cycle time. Add a regression test that proves a slow-but-working runner (5 minutes of agent_status: working with lifecycle: in-progress) does NOT trip the stalled lifecycle.

WP3 — Chat-driven autopilot ergonomics. Add mp autopilot wait <id> that blocks until the milestone reaches complete (or failed / cancelled), with a configurable timeout (default 30 min). Add mp autopilot tail <id> --follow --since=<ts> that streams recent activity events (from master-plan/activity.json) for the given session, optionally following in real time. Both surface the existing live-detached session without requiring a fresh mp autopilot start. The two new verbs round out the chat-friendly workflow alongside the existing mp autopilot status snapshot.
out_of_scope: A full chat-side tool integration (i.e., exposing the autopilot as a tool that the chat agent can call as a function). That's a separate feature milestone, not M246.

Re-architecting the runner pane management (herdr pane split / agent start timing). The 6 herdr-0.9.x drift patches in commit ebe1cfc are the right baseline; M246 is what the orchestrator does once panes are running.
Adding a new harness (claude, codex, etc.) to the autopilot. The harness registry's V1 set is opencode / cursor / pi; a new entry is a follow-up.
Changing the autopilot's UI in raul (the M241 / M242 / M245 milestones cover that). M246 is server-side only — pure autopilot, no UI surface.

acceptance_criteria.description: Runner-readiness gate fires before the prompt is delivered. After mp autopilot start <id>, the orchestrator's send_prompt call to the runner blocks until agent_status == idle (with the configured grace). A unit test stubs the runner's interactive_ready response and asserts the prompt queue depth is non-zero before the gate clears and zero after.

A slow-but-working runner does NOT trip the stalled lifecycle. A test simulates agent_status: working + lifecycle: in-progress for 5 minutes; the poller must keep the lifecycle in in-progress, not transition to stalled.

mp autopilot wait <id> blocks until the milestone reaches complete. A test runs the autopilot on a fake milestone; the wait subprocess returns exit 0 within the configured timeout when the milestone completes, and exit 1 with a structured error when the timeout elapses.

mp autopilot tail <id> --follow streams recent activity events. A test seeds activity.json with a known sequence, invokes tail (without --follow so it terminates after the existing entries), and asserts the output matches the seed in order. A second test with --follow against an in-process appender runs the loop and exits when no new events arrive for 500 ms.

stall_timeout_minutes config knob is honored. The test sets agent.automation.stall_timeout_minutes = 1 and asserts the configured value is what the state-machine reads. A second test sets it to 60 and confirms the read.
make lint, make test, and consumer-surface-lint all stay green; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings exits 0.
acceptance_criteria.verification: make lint && make test && make consumer-surface-lint

work_packages.name: Runner-readiness gate
work_packages.goal: Before the orchestrator dispatches the runner prompt, wait for the runner's interactive_ready: true plus a configurable grace period. The gate is a single wait_for_runner_idle(grace_ms) call in the prompt-dispatch path.
work_packages.rollback: Revert the gate call; the dispatcher sends the prompt immediately as before.

work_packages.name: Lifecycle poller stall threshold
work_packages.goal: Tune the default stall window from 30 min to 5 min, with a config override agent.automation.stall_timeout_minutes (range 1..120, default 5). A slow-but-working runner must not trip the stalled lifecycle.
work_packages.rollback: Revert the default to 30 min and drop the config knob; the test that asserts the timeout is honored still passes because the absolute value is irrelevant to the test.

work_packages.name: Chat-driven autopilot ergonomics (wait / tail)
work_packages.goal: Add two new subcommands under mp autopilot: wait <id> blocks until the milestone reaches a terminal lifecycle (complete / failed / cancelled) with a configurable timeout; tail <id> [--follow] [--since <ts>] streams recent activity events for the named session.
work_packages.rollback: Drop both new subcommands; mp autopilot status and reading activity.json by hand remain the only way to observe a detached session.

steps.action: Implement wait_for_runner_idle(grace_ms) in crates/mp/src/autopilot/drive/bridge.rs. The function calls herdr agent get <runner_pane> and waits for agent_status == idle (with interactive_ready: true), polling at the configured poll interval. Default grace is 5000 ms; a negative grace disables the post-idle delay.

Add the agent.automation.stall_timeout_minutes config knob in crates/mp/src/config.rs (default 5, range 1..120). Read the value in crates/mp/src/autopilot/drive/state_machine.rs and use it in the stall transition. Update the default from 30 min to 5 min.

Add mp autopilot wait <id> subcommand. Reads the run-state file in a poll loop; exits 0 when the milestone reaches complete, exit 1 with a structured error when the timeout elapses (default 30 min, override via --timeout <sec>). Print the final lifecycle on success.

Add mp autopilot tail <id> [--follow] [--since <ts>] subcommand. Without --follow, reads the run's recent activity events from master-plan/activity.json and prints them. With --follow, polls activity.json for new events (per the lane's last_id) and prints them as they're appended, exiting after --idle <sec> of no new events (default 5 sec).

Wire the readiness gate into the prompt-dispatch path in crates/mp/src/autopilot/drive/state_machine.rs. Replace the immediate send_prompt call with a wait_for_runner_idle(grace_ms); send_prompt sequence. Default grace is read from the existing mp autopilot start config.

Add a regression test that simulates a runner at agent_status: working + lifecycle: in-progress for 5 minutes and asserts the poller does NOT transition to stalled. Use a deterministic clock injection so the test runs in milliseconds, not minutes.

Update the existing mp autopilot status help text to cross-reference the new wait and tail verbs, and update docs/commands/autopilot.md to document both. Add CHANGELOG entry under Unreleased: mp autopilot: new wait / tail verbs; runner-readiness gate; configurable stall window (default 5 min).

Add a regression test that runs the full pipeline on a fake runner (a stub herdr agent get that reports agent_status: busy for the first 3 polls, then idle after a simulated 2-second build). Asserts the prompt is queued (not delivered) during the busy window and delivered after the gate clears.

Add a regression test that simulates a runner at agent_status: working + lifecycle: in-progress for 5 minutes and asserts the poller does NOT transition to stalled. Use a deterministic clock injection so the test runs in milliseconds, not minutes.

Update the existing mp autopilot status help text to cross-reference the new wait and tail verbs, and update docs/commands/autopilot.md to document both. Add CHANGELOG entry under Unreleased: mp autopilot: new wait / tail verbs; runner-readiness gate; configurable stall window (default 5 min).

Add the AC-05 config-knob test: set agent.automation.stall_timeout_minutes = 1 and assert the state-machine reads that exact value. A second test sets it to 60 and confirms the read. Both tests are deterministic (no real waiting).
